title: Apply Cellpose: saved masks and live-filter checks
description: Apply stock CPSAM to three downloadable real images through the nested Workbench, inspect native figures and console output, and test live filters without confusing preview with batch inference.
objectives: Find Apply inside Make Masks and its Cellpose Workbench.
Use the recorded source, channel and stock-model settings on preserved real-image copies.
Inspect the three actual saved masks and their original, outline and flow figures.
Demonstrate reversible live filtering and synchronized wheel zoom.
Recognise the measured preview-versus-batch mismatch and avoid accuracy claims.
prerequisite: Extract the linked three-image example into a new directory and set src to its images folder; recorded_settings.json contains historical resolved values, not a demonstrated portable GUI import. These real 512-square uint16 cell crops are not ground truth. Stock CPSAM is selected, not the Train lesson checkpoint. Batch choices are channels=[0], normalize=True, percentiles=[2,99], diameter=30, CP_prob=0, flow_threshold=0.4, batch_size=1, save=True and verbose=True; rescale, resample, resize, fill_in, invert and remove_background are False. The actual CUDA run saves 9/94/46 labels and three GUI figures. Direct reference calls independently reproduce all mask pixels and all three figure arrays. Outlines show external foreground contours, not every touching instance border; the flow panel is one visualization channel, not measured motion. Live preview of image 02 yields 95, not 94: it matches raw-image Cellpose defaults rather than the batch preprocessing/resampling path. Displayed 2/99 controls do not establish equivalence. Area cutoff 1838 gives 95->47->95, every restored pixel checked without model rerun; saved batch masks are unchanged. Native wheel zoom synchronizes both canvases but crops the view and does not fix the narrow preview card. Earlier holds and source data remain preserved. No biological accuracy certification, AI request, publication or application modification.

scenes.narration: From Make Masks, open the nested Cellpose Workbench and choose Apply. Train and Apply share this workbench; Apply is not a separate Home tile. This lesson uses the stock model on three real images. It does not use the demonstration checkpoint from the linked Train lesson.

Extract the linked example into a new folder. Set source to its images directory, preserving the original download. These are three single-channel cell images, each five hundred twelve pixels square. They are demonstration inputs, not segmentation ground truth. Use the recorded settings as a reference, replacing the historical source path with your own.

Select CPSAM and leave custom model empty. For these images, the channel list is zero, normalization uses the second and ninety-ninth percentiles, diameter is thirty, flow threshold is zero point four, and cell probability is zero. These are bounded example choices, not recommended settings for every experiment.

With Save and Verbose enabled and batch size one, run Apply. This route creates figures without a separate Plot switch. The real console identifies an RTX thirty-ninety using CUDA and finishes all three images. Check the source and saved settings there; a Finished message alone is not an accuracy measurement.

Three same-named mask TIFFs are saved in the source folder's masks subdirectory. The counts are nine, ninety-four and forty-six. These genuine figures show the input, red foreground contours and a flow visualization. The contours do not trace every touching instance boundary, and flow colours are not physical motion or segmentation accuracy.

Turn on Live preview and use its actual image picker to choose cell pair zero two. Collapse Console and System when you need more viewing space. Preview has its own controls: check channel zero and the displayed percentile values in Live settings rather than assuming every Apply option was copied.

This preview finds ninety-five objects, while the saved batch mask for the same image has ninety-four. Independent checks reproduce both results: the preview follows Cellpose's raw-image defaults, not the batch's explicit preprocessing and resampling choices. Treat it as an exploratory view, not a guarantee of identical saved masks.

The preview card remains narrow in this build. Wheel zoom enlarges a detail on both canvases together; it does not enlarge the card, and the full image is now cropped. This is useful for inspecting local outlines, but keep whole-field review separate from a zoomed detail.

Open Live settings and set the minimum cell area to eighteen hundred thirty-eight pixels. This is a demonstration cutoff, not an optimal biological threshold. Close the dialog to see the result. The live filter removes forty-eight objects, leaving forty-seven, without rerunning Cellpose or changing its raw segmentation.

Here is the filtered preview with the dialog closed and wheel zoom reapplied. The original image is unchanged while small mask objects disappear. The counter now says forty-seven. These changes affect the preview; they do not rewrite the three batch TIFFs already saved on disk.

Return minimum area to zero, close the dialog and inspect again. Ninety-five objects return, and every restored label pixel matches the baseline. Keep the inputs, settings and model identity with the saved masks. The optional spaCR AI console is unused here; independent validation remains your responsibility before drawing scientific conclusions.
